headline: Anthropic has agreed a deal to license technology from the AI-security company Opaque and take on part of its team, in what is known as an acqui-hire.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a small team-and-licence deal that fits Anthropic's push into enterprise customers, with terms undisclosed.
importance_line: Enterprise customers that want to run AI on their own premises with strong data protection could gain from Anthropic adding Opaque's technology, and some of Opaque's staff move to a larger company, but the terms, the number of staff joining and Anthropic's own account are not public.
summary: Constellation Research reports that Anthropic will license technology from Opaque, a company that built confidential-computing software (technology that keeps data protected while an AI model is processing it), and take on some of its team in an acqui-hire, a deal that buys a team and a licence rather than the whole company; terms were not disclosed, and Opaque's chief executive, Aaron Fulkerson, announced the agreement in a post. Constellation says the deal fits Anthropic's growing effort to win enterprises that want on-premises deployments, open models and sovereign AI (AI kept under an organisation's or country's own control); Opaque had raised a $24 million Series B round at a $300 million valuation and partnered with Nvidia, Intel, Microsoft and Google.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. "Acqui-hire" explanation and the plain-English gloss of confidential computing and sovereign AI are the desk's.
